stories.notes: Cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with zero acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Requires openspec to elaborate AC, define technical approach for real-time preview rendering, and propose story splits per platform. Speckit must follow to harden testability criteria, security around preview content rendering, and edge cases (e.g., offline, auth, large content). High complexity and cross-platform scope warrant both agents.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new live-preview capability for Contentstack CMS content. No acceptance criteria provided; VCs derived from the description. The useContent hook (236 callers) is the single integration point through which all content flows — attaching live-preview subscription there propagates to every consumer without modifying individual components. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are framed at our boundary with mocked Contentstack client.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so all 10 criteria above are new. I derived them from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the four named files (useContent hook as the single integration point, contentstack service as the client, contentCard interface as the data contract, ContentstackLink as a leaf consumer), and openspec's own notes about the useContent hook being the 236-caller integration point. AC-1/2 cover the core live-preview happy path. AC-3 ensures non-preview mode is unaffected. AC-4 guards interface integrity after live updates. AC-5 covers subscription failure. AC-6 addresses ContentstackLink specifically named in the tech notes. AC-7 adds the partial/malformed-update edge case. AC-8 prevents production performance regression. AC-9 ensures subscription cleanup on unmount (memory-leak prevention). AC-10 addresses security (no credential leakage). CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents — the criteria are based solely on the story description and file names. If the current useContent hook already has partial live-preview support, some criteria may already be satisfied and should be adjusted.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths confirmed to exist — no missing paths, no missing_manifest_path flag. Brownfield story: empty acceptanceCriteria array is immutable; both agents correctly report acceptanceChanged=false and splitCount=0, so no split or AC-mutation evaluation applies. OpenSpec added meaningful, non-overlapping value: identified useContent hook as the 236-caller single integration point, framed verification conditions at the Contentstack boundary with a mocked client, and provided plausible technical context for the live-preview approach. Speckit's contribution is internally contradictory and unreliable. Its notes claim 'all 10 criteria above are new' and describe each one (AC-1 through AC-10), but the story's acceptanceCriteria array is empty [] — those 10 criteria do not exist in the artefact under review. This is either a hallucination or a persistence failure where speckit's output was never written back. The acceptanceChanged=false flag directly contradicts the claim of creating 10 new ACs. Additionally, speckit admits it 'could not read the actual file contents,' meaning its derived criteria are based solely on filenames and the story title rather than actual code — undermining the reliability of the criteria even if they had been persisted. Human review is needed to: (1) determine whether the 10 criteria were persisted in a separate spec file and simply not surfaced in the story JSON, or were never applied at all; (2) verify the criteria are grounded in actual file contents; (3) reconcile the acceptanceChanged=false flag with speckit's claim of new AC creation.
